item.title: Liam Coen: Colts traded away two good players right before we play them, can't deny that
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen acknowledged that his team's task got a little easier when the Colts traded away two of their top players, offensive lineman Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen acknowledged that his team's task got a little easier when the Colts traded away two of their top players, offensive lineman Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. The Jaguars face the Colts on Sunday, and now it's a Colts team that has turned its attention away from winning this year and toward building for the future.

But Coen also cautioned that the Jaguars can't allow themselves to be thinking about what's going on with the Colts.

"Obviously really good players that I have a lot of respect for. Quenton Nelson was playing some of the best football of his career, as was Buckner in a lot of ways — extremely disruptive in both the run and the pass, tipped balls, created some issues inside," Coen said. "It's two good players, you can't deny that. But knowing what that team is going to want to do, this has to all be about our improvements, us getting back on track. Got a good division opponent that we're playing at home, and the focus level, getting in pads today, has to be about our execution, our fundamentals and technique, because you can't control that stuff and if you think about it too much it typically doesn't help."

Asked if he thought the Colts might trade Jonathan Taylor, too, Coen indicated that he doesn't think that's going to happen.

"You try not to get into that world because it's just rat poison either way," Coen said. "And also a part of you wants to beat good teams, you want to beat opponents that provide strong competition, as this team does."

Coen wants his players to remember that the Colts team that shows up on Sunday will be playing to win.

"Philly a couple weeks ago had a lot of guys out and played us to the last second," Coen said. "In this league, any given Sunday, we all know anything can happen."

item.title: Jerry Jones: Troy Aikman working for Cowboys in future is "very possible"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Troy Aikman was in Philadelphia to call Monday night's game between the Cowboys and the Eagles and he took some time before it got underway to catch up with his first boss in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Troy Aikman was in Philadelphia to call Monday night's game between the Cowboys and the Eagles and he took some time before it got underway to catch up with his first boss in the NFL.

Aikman's conversation with Cowboys owner Jerry Jones before the Dallas win comes at a moment of professional uncertainty for Aikman. His contract with ESPN will be up at the end of the season and he recently said he would "have a hard time not taking a good look" at a chance to work for the organization that drafted him with the first overall pick in 1989.

Aikman has worked as a consultant for the Dolphins and Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday if he's open to the idea of Aikman taking on a significant role in the organization. Jones said he "could and would" be open to that notion and called Aikman "certainly qualified" to take on that kind of job.

"He’s one of the hardest working, most focused people that I’ve ever been around," Jones said. "When you’re around each other, a part of that makeup can make it where you have your ups and downs. I think the world of him. I’ve seen his image and had it in my eyes since I walked in the NFL. He's outstanding. The answer is not necessarily that we're going to do something more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It is very possible."

Very possible and definitely happening are far from the same thing, but smoke signals about a possible partnership could prove to be foreshadowing for what will take place when and if it becomes definite that Aikman is going to be looking for a new job come the end of the 2026 season.

item.title: Some owners are spending big on the midterm elections
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With all the talk about asses and advertisements, it's easy to forget that a fairly important election is coming in six days.
item.content:encoded:
With all the talk about asses and advertisements, it's easy to forget that a fairly important election is coming in six days.

Plenty of NFL owners are very much aware.

The folks at Front Office Sports have compiled a list of donations made by the people who hold the paper on pro football franchises, based on data from the Federal Election Commission.

The total is more than $18 million, with nearly half of that amount coming from one person. Rob Walton of the Broncos has given $8.95 million, primarily to Republican candidates and political action committees.

New Seahawks owner Vinod Kholsa has given $2.09 million, primarily to Democratic causes. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has donated $1.81 million, primarily to Republican causes. Browns owners Jimmy and Dee Haslam have given $1.56 million, primarily to Republican causes. No owners have given more than $1 million.

Of the top 12 owners who wrote checks to candidates, 10 of them primarily gave to Republican candidates and PACs. Which makes sense. More than anything else, rich people tend to gravitate toward a political philosophy based on lower taxes.

item.title: Report: Jaylen Waddle aggravated previous chest injury, Week 8 status TBD
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Broncos head coach Sean Payton criticized himself for the play call that ended with receiver Jaylen Waddle suffering a chest injury.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos head coach Sean Payton criticized himself for the play call that ended with receiver Jaylen Waddle suffering a chest injury.

There’s now more information available about Waddle’s potential availability for Week 8.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Waddle suffered an aggravation of his previous chest injury on the play and his status for Sunday’s game against Kansas City will be determined later.

Whether or not he plays will be based on his practice participation this week.

Waddle, who arrived in Denver via offseason trade, has likely not been as productive as the team envisioned in 2026. While he caught eight passes for 138 yards in the Week 2 win over Jacksonville, he has not eclipsed 50 yards in a game since.

In all, Waddle has 26 receptions for 276 yards with one TD through seven games.

item.title: Giants GM Joe Schoen on trades: We're looking, but has to make sense now and in future
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants hit their bye week in first place in the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record and that's made the prospect of bolstering the roster in the trade market a popular topic of conversation around the team.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants hit their bye week in first place in the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record and that's made the prospect of bolstering the roster in the trade market a popular topic of conversation around the team.

On Tuesday, General Manager Joe Schoen said at a press conference that the team's players have "earned the right" to play in meaningful games in the final weeks of the season and that means the Giants will "canvas the league" to see if there are ways to increase the chances of that happening. Schoen t tcautioned that any potential move will have to fit both the team's immediate needs as well as their future prospects.

"There's a lot of factors into it, in terms of where we are pick-wise," Schoen said, via a transcript from the team. "We don't have a fourth or a fifth right now. So, you take that into account. In some situations, that may rule some players out. Maybe that's what their value is. Maybe a third is too rich or a sixth isn't enough, so then you start looking into future picks and contract status, where we are depth-wise. . . . So, we're going to look at all the options that are available. And there's certain teams that have already started some trades and we've been in contact with those teams and have a pretty good idea of who may or may not be available. And again, it's got to make sense, short-term and long-term, when you make those moves."

The Colts got the ball rolling on trade season by dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Tuesday. That will likely spark more conversations as teams try to avoid being without a chair when the music stops, but Schoen's balancing act won't be an easy one if it turns out to be a seller's market around the league.

item.title: Chiefs to sign Justin Tucker to their practice squad
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Tucker has been out of the league since being released by the Ravens in May 2025.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Tucker is back in the NFL.

Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star reports that the Chiefs will sign Tucker to their practice squad. The veteran kicker has worked out for a number of teams over the last two years, but has not been on any active roster or practice squad since being released by the Ravens in May 2025.

Tucker's release came after he was accused of sexual misconduct by a number of massage therapists. He was suspended for the first 10 games of the 2025 season as a result of those allegations.

Tucker spent 13 seasons with the Ravens and was one of the league's top kickers for most of that stretch. He is 17th in points scored and has the second-best field goal percentage in NFL history.

Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker is fifth all-time in field goal percentage, but is just 11-of-16 on field goals this season.

item.title: Jerry Jones thinks it is "unlikely" Cowboys add help in a trade
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The trade deadline is a couple of weeks away, but things started heating up on Tuesday with the Colts making a pair of trades that could spur other teams to start making moves as well.
item.content:encoded:
The trade deadline is a couple of weeks away, but things started heating up on Tuesday with the Colts making a pair of trades that could spur other teams to start making moves as well.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has never been shy when it comes to talking about his willingness to make deals in hopes of improving his roster and he's been particularly vocal about his desire to bolster the defense in Dallas this year. That desire wasn't satiated by their early move to add cornerback Joey Porter Jr., but Jones said on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday that he doesn't think anything else is going to come together for the Cowboys.

"If we could do it where we sit right now, I would add to it," Jones said, via the team's website. "But the adding to it is a big statement. It's unlikely we'll get the opportunity from outside coming in. But if it's there, I'll do it."

There's enough time left before November 10 for something to develop, but Jones thinks the Cowboys are going to have to play out the rest of the schedule with what's already on hand.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's a new no. 1, by default.
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 3; 5-1): For the first time ever, a team ascends to No. 1 without playing.

2. Jaguars (No. 4; 4-2): For the first time ever, a team ascends to No. 2 without playing.

3. Vikings (No. 5; 6-0): A four-game gauntlet is coming.

4. 49ers (No. 1; 6-1): The bye week came at the best possible time.

5. Chiefs (No. 2; 5-1): They badly need help at receiver.

6. Broncos (No. 6; 5-2): Take that, Ryan Fitzpatrick.

7. Seahawks (No. 7; 4-3): Can they do to Caleb Williams what they did to Patrick Mahomes?

8. Bears (No. 10; 5-2): The NFC Championship matchup we almost got in January happens on Monday night.

9. Browns (No. 11; 5-2): If they can complete the sweep of the Steelers, they'll control the division.

10. Steelers (No. 13; 5-2): Sunday's home game against Cleveland is the closest thing to a "must" win that any 5-2 team will ever have.

11. Patriots (No. 8; 4-3): With the Packers and Lions looming, they can't overlook the Dolphins.

12. Bengals (No. 14; 4-2): Ja'Marr Chase's halftime speech may have saved the season.

13. Lions (No. 18; 4-2): Can Jared Goff figure out the Brian Flores defense?

14. Packers (No. 9; 4-3): They can't let one loss become two on Thursday night.

15. Ravens (No. 12; 4-3): It feels like the entire season hinges on the next two games (at Bills, Jaguars).

16. Rams (No. 17; 3-4): If they can keep running the ball the way they did on Sunday, they can start stacking wins.

17. Giants (No. 21; 4-2-1): They're becoming the most fun team to watch in the entire league.

18. Falcons (No. 24; 3-4): More Jekyll, less Hyde.

19. Raiders (No. 16; 3-4): Mendoza time is coming.

20. Buccaneers (No. 29; 2-5): The NFC South is still theirs for the taking.

21. Cowboys (No. 23; 3-4): The best solution for a bad defense is an offense that stays on the field for as long as it can.

22. Panthers (No. 15; 3-3): Drinks are on the house.

23. Texans (No. 19; 2-5): Has an elite defense ever fallen apart this quickly?

24. Saints (No. 20; 2-5): The win over the Giants may have saved Kellen Moore from a bye-week buh-bye.

25. Cardinals (No. 22; 2-5): It's Carson Beck time.

26. Eagles (No. 25; 2-5): Lose to the 1-4-1 Commanders on Sunday night, and this season is over. (It may be anyway.)

27. Titans (No. 26; 1-6): Will they ever win two in a row again?

28. Colts (No. 27; 2-5): The trade deadline could get very interesting.

29. Dolphins (No. 31; 1-5): Only five weeks until the next Jets game.

30. Commanders (No. 30; 1-4-1): Did Dan Quinn know it was the bye week?

31. Jets (No. 28; 2-5): The clock is ticking on Aaron Glenn.

32. Chargers (No. 32; 0-6): "Last winless team in the league" wasn't mentioned in their schedule-release video.

item.title: Broadcast home for Monday night wild-card game still isn't known
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As we close in on the 50-percent mark (that's half, for those unfamiliar with the concept of percentages) of the regular season nearly in the can, the playoffs are coming.
item.content:encoded:
As we close in on the 50-percent mark (that's half, for those unfamiliar with the concept of percentages) of the regular season nearly in the can, the playoffs are coming. And it's still not known where the last game of the first round will be televised.

In 2021, the NFL moved one of the six wild-card games to Monday night. ESPN has been the exclusive home for the Monday night playoff game. ESPN's contractual right to that expired last year.

As noted by Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing, the TGL schedule on ESPN highlights the uncertainty as to whether ESPN will, or won't, be televising an NFL game on Monday night, January 18.

Last year, Fox, CBS, NBC, Prime Video, and ESPN televised wild-card games. If the Monday night game remains available to anyone, any of them could land the game — for the right price.

It's also possible, in theory, that Netflix could swoop in and snatch the game. That's how Netflix has been unveiling its NFL strategy in recent years. When no one expects it, boom, here's Netflix with another game to "eventize."

The Monday night game would fit the current Netflix aspirations. And, with six first-round games and six partners at the table, each of them could end up with one wild-card game.

For fans, it doesn't matter much. The game will be on somewhere. For the networks, the prospect of getting the Monday night game matters plenty.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Lions head coach Dan Campbell offered updates on Monday about a couple of players who emerged from Sunday's win over the Packers with ankle injuries.
item.content:encoded:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell offered updates on Monday about a couple of players who emerged from Sunday's win over the Packers with ankle injuries.

Campbell said there was optimism that wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw will both be able to play in next Sunday's home game against the Vikings, but that their practice work will be managed to keep them on track.

"I think those guys will probably sit Wednesday," Campbell said. "The plan is to get them going Thursday and I think they’ll be fine. They should be good, we’ll see when we get there."

St. Brown had nine catches for 153 yards while playing 78 percent of the offensive snaps. Rakestraw was limited to 21 snaps and recorded two tackles.

item.title: Vikings register highest blitz rate of Next Gen Stats era, at 85.2 percent
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The blitz-happy Vikings defense took their habit to the highest level on Sunday against the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
The blitz-happy Vikings defense took their habit to the highest level on Sunday against the Colts.

Via NBC Sports research, Minnesota blitzed on 85.2 percent of the Colts' dropbacks on Sunday. It was the highest rate by any team in the Next Gen Stats era, which dates back to 2016.

The effort limited the Colts to 64 net passing yards, thanks to four sacks that erased 44 yards.

The challenge comes from the confusion created by the Brian Flores defense. The offense never knows who is and isn't coming until the snap. It forces the blockers to quickly diagnose the situation, and it requires the quarterback to process his reads before he gets knocked down.

Minnesota needed that. The run defense wasn't getting it done on Sunday; the Colts gained 154 yards on the ground. By the time the final drive came, the Colts had no choice but to throw — and Minnesota's relentlessness forced quarterback Daniel Jones into his lone turnover of the day, a game-sealing interception.

And that was enough to deliver a 16-10 win, moving the Vikings to 6-0 for the first time since 2009. While also extending Minnesota's winning streak to 11, the second longest in franchise history.

item.title: Report: Aaron Jones considered day-to-day with knee injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There is some positive news on the injury front for the undefeated Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
There is some positive news on the injury front for the undefeated Vikings.

While running back Aaron Jones had to depart Sunday's win over the Colts with a knee injury, it is not considered to be significant at this time, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.

Jones was described as day-to-day.

Jones has been dealing with injury issues throughout 2026, but has not yet missed a game. He has rushed for 436 yards with two touchdowns and caught 13 passes for 72 yards.

Jones departed Sunday’s game having rushed for 26 yards on eight carries. Jordan Mason had the bulk of the work at running back, rushing for 68 yards on 15 attempts.

The 6-0 Vikings will be on the road to face the 4-2 Lions on Sunday afternoon in Week 8.

item.title: Kevin O'Connell: We're confident we're not far off offensively
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: With the 49ers and Chiefs losing on Sunday, the Vikings are the last unbeaten team standing in the NFL and they are in some rare company when it comes to how they're winning games.
item.content:encoded:
With the 49ers and Chiefs losing on Sunday, the Vikings are the last unbeaten team standing in the NFL and they are in some rare company when it comes to how they're winning games.

The Vikings have scored 10 touchdowns in their six wins and, per ESPN, they are tied for the third-fewest touchdowns during a 6-0 start in NFL history. On Sunday, the team scored its only touchdown to take their first lead of the day in the fourth quarter and they finished their 16-10 win over the Colts with 275 yards of offense.

After the game, head coach Kevin O'Connell pointed out near misses in the passing game and penalties as things that kept the offense from finding a groove and said that there's strong belief that things are going to fall into place.

"I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going."

The Vikings will kick off November with a trip to Detroit before moving on to face the Bills, Packers, 49ers and Falcons over the rest of the month. That makes it an ideal time for them to make a move from "not far off" to clicking in a way that will allow them to remain at the front of the NFC playoff race.

item.title: With two trades in one day, Colts are clearly open for business
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Sunday Splash!
item.content:encoded:
The Sunday Splash! report regarding a potential fire sale in Indy was conditioned on the Colts’ performance in their three remaining games before the trade deadline. After only one game, they tapped the "Everything Must Go" sign in the front yard.

Guard Quenton Nelson, as expected, has been traded to the Seahawks. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner has been traded back to the 49ers, as expected.

So who's next? Running back Jonathan Taylor has been the focal point of speculation, with ESPN linking him to the Packers, Seahawks, Broncos, and Vikings.

The Vikings got the ultimate opportunity to scout Taylor on Sunday, when he accounted for 110 of the team's 218 total offensive yards in a 16-10 Minnesota win. Taylor averaged 5.3 yards per carry and went 38 yards for the Colts' only touchdown of the day.

There's an obvious incentive to maximize 2027 draft picks, especially with the Colts' first-rounder committed to the Jets as the back end of the Sauce Gardner trade. But Taylor is under contract for two more years; they may want to keep him until the offseason, giving the next G.M. the opportunity to decide whether to retain Taylor or trade him in March.

Of course, Taylor would have more value now to a team that hopes to augment its roster for a playoff push. Although the Vikings were burned 37 years ago this month by the Herschel Walker trade, it would take much less than the ridiculous haul of picks and players (which became more picks after the Cowboys cut them) to get Taylor.

Taylor could make a huge difference for a team premised on a stout defense. While Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason have proven to be capable options at tailback, Taylor is among the best in the league. He has the power and speed to move the chains and, when given an opening, go the distance.

Whatever happens with Taylor, it's clear the Colts aren't waiting to see what happens over the next two weekends. In a deadline-driven business, the timeline for the Colts isn't being driven by the deadline. It's being determined by getting deals done now and moving on.

item.title: Malik Beasley agrees to plead guilty to gambling charges
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Veteran NBA guard Malik Beasley, who was indicted earlier this year for federal gambling crimes, will be revising his not-guilty plea.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran NBA guard Malik Beasley, who was indicted earlier this year for federal gambling crimes, will be revising his not-guilty plea.

Per Mike Vorkunov of The Athletic, Beasley will be pleading guilty.

The formal charges were filed in June. Beasley was accused of participating in a scheme based on manipulation of prop bets based on his statistics.

Beasley is scheduled to officially plead guilty on December 9.

The nine-year veteran allegedly manipulated his play in four games with the Milwaukee Bucks during the 2023-24 season. He allegedly agreed to do so as a way to pay off a loan after falling into debt.

Beasley, 29, spent nine seasons in the NBA. He earned roughly $60 million. Per Vorkunov, Beasley nearly signed a new $42 million deal after finishing second in the Sixth Man of the Year voting for the 2024-25 season. The offer was withdrawn after the gambling situation came to light.

The Beasley situation is just one of several NBA gambling scandals since sports betting became legalized on a widespread basis. The NFL has avoided, to date, a major gambling scandal since the Supreme Court opened the floodgates in 2018 to state-by-state wagering on sports.

item.title: 49ers agree to acquire DeForest Buckner from Colts
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Buckner is headed back to the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.
item.content:encoded:
DeForest Buckner is headed back to the Bay.

The 49ers — who traded Buckner to Indianapolis back in 2020 — have agreed to acquire Buckner from the Colts, according to multiple reports.

Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick to complete the deal.

While Buckner is in his 11th season, he’s still plenty productive from the interior of the defensive line. He’s recorded 4.0 sacks with four tackles for loss and eight QB hits so far in 2026. He’s also tallied three passes defensed and a fumble recovery.

The No. 7 overall pick of the 2016 draft out of Oregon, Buckner was a key piece of San Francisco’s defense in his first four seasons, helping the club advance to Super Bowl LIV to cap the 2019 season. He registered 12.0 sacks for the 49ers in 2018 and 7.5 sacks for the club in 2019.

He was traded to the Colts after his fourth season, with Indianapolis signing him to a long-term second contract.

In Buckner’s 158 career games, he’s picked up 75.5 sacks, 101 tackles for loss, and 196 QB hits.

Buckner has been palpably frustrated by the Colts losses in recent weeks. With an expiring contract, it's no surprise that he's been moved.

It's the second high-profile trade of the day from the Colts, who earlier dealt guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks.

item.title: Jessie Bates: You can sleep well at night when Michael Penix is your QB
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: It took longer than the Falcons would have hoped, but Michael Penix has now been a starting quarterback for the equivalent of a full season.
item.content:encoded:
It took longer than the Falcons would have hoped, but Michael Penix has now been a starting quarterback for the equivalent of a full season.

Last Sunday's 29-20 win over the 49ers was his 17th NFL start and Penix had one of his better games in that outing. He was 25-of-34 for 213 yards and three touchdowns as the Falcons moved to 7-10 in his starts.

While that record could be better, Penix's individual numbers back up the promise the Falcons saw in him coming out of Washington. Penix has thrown for 3,876 yards, 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions while completing 61.5 percent of his passes. In his five starts this season, Penix has helped the Falcons to 31 points a game, which is tops in the league over that span, and he's convinced safety Jessie Bates that he's the right man for the job.

"When No. 9 is out there, this team is a completely different football team and I really truly believe that he is a franchise quarterback. . . . You can sleep good at night when you have Michael Penix playing quarterback for you," Bates said this week, via the team's website.

The Falcons are 3-2 since Penix returned from last season's torn ACL and a win over the Buccaneers this weekend would leave them at 4-4 on the season. It would also have them in first place in the NFC South if the Panthers lose to the Packers on Thursday night, which would be a good step toward convincing others that Bates's assessment is on the mark.

item.title: Chad Kelly becomes the first million-dollar player of CFL salary-cap era
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Quarterback Chad Kelly said earlier this year that he'd still like to return to the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Chad Kelly said earlier this year that he’d still like to return to the NFL. For now, he'll continue to play in the CFL.

And he'll be paid more than any player in the Canadian league's salary-cap era.

Via Justin Dunk of 3DownNation.com, Kelly's new five-year, $5.55 million contract with the Toronto Argonauts makes him the first million-dollar player since the CFL implemented a team-by-team spending limit.

Kelly, now 32, was due to become a free agent after the current season.

Nathan Rourke was the CFL's highest-paid player in 2026, at a salary of $684,700. Kelly ranked second, at $625,000.

Kelly was the last pick of the 2017 draft. After his NFL career fizzled out, in 2020, he landed in the CFL in 2022 and has flourished there.

To date, he has had no opportunities to follow in the footsteps of Warren Moon, Doug Flutie, Jeff Garcia, Joe Theismann, and Joe Kapp as quarterbacks who parlayed CFL success into NFL careers. At some point, why wouldn't a team in the quarterback-needy NFL give Kelly a look?

item.title: Robert Griffin III wants to be the next Baylor coach
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: From time to time, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III expresses interest in continuing his career.
item.content:encoded:
From time to time, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III expresses interest in continuing his career. He's now inteested in embarking on a new path entirely.

Earlier this week, Griffin said he'd like to become the next head coach at Baylor.

"Yes, 100 percent," Griffin told Dan Patrick on Monday, via ESPN. "If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn't just respectable on the football field, but the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor. So yeah, I would 100 percent be interested."

Griffin won the Heisman Trophy at Baylor in 2011. In 2012, he became the second overall pick in the NFL draft. The NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Year, a knee injury derailed his career in Washington. By his fourth year, he was benched for Kirk Cousins.

In 2016, he played for the Browns. Out of football in 2017, he spent his final three seasons with the Ravens. He last played in 2020.

Baylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday, after going 40-40 in six-plus seasons.

More than a few former players have become college football coaches in recent years. Typically, their careers start at a lower-level program. Especially when, like Griffin, they have no coaching experience.

Earlier this week, former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers, who has been a high-school football coach in Alabama since 2021, was named as a potential candidate at NC State, where he played before becoming the fourth overall pick in the 2004 draft.

Since his playing career ended, Griffin has worked for ESPN and Fox.

item.title: Texas left tackle and likely first-round pick Trevor Goosby out for season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby, a likely first-round draft pick and the protector of Arch Manning's blind side, will miss the rest of this season with a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby, a likely first-round draft pick and the protector of Arch Manning's blind side, will miss the rest of this season with a knee injury.

Goosby suffered the injury on Saturday against Ole Miss. The exact nature of the injury has not been revealed, but Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Goosby's knee doesn't look good, and Pete Thamel of ESPN reported that he won't play again this season.

The 6-foot-7, 325-pound Goosby currently ranks 15th in the betting odds to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. First overall now seems extremely unlikely, but unless the injury is very severe, he still looks like a safe bet to be a first-round pick.

Goosby could also, however, decide to keep playing college football in 2027. He still has a year of NCAA eligibility left, and he is believed to be making more than $1 million in NIL this year. The combination of an even more lucrative NIL deal next year and the chance to bolster his draft stock with an even better season in 2027 may entice him to return to college and wait until 2028 to enter the NFL draft.

Manning, who has had an up-and-down season at Texas this year, may struggle without Goosby protecting him, and that will also make an impact on Manning's status. Manning entered this season as the favorite to go first overall in the 2027 NFL draft, but his play this year has not justified that hype, and there's now talk that Manning could stay in college in 2027 and focus on the 2028 draft.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs closing in on 6,000 scrimmage yards and 60 touchdowns in four NFL seasons
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Gibbs is set to become the third player in NFL history to reach those milestones within his first four years in the league.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday against the Vikings, Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs could join an elite club in NFL history.

Gibbs has 5,919 scrimmage yards and 58 scrimmage touchdowns since the Lions drafted him in 2023, so as soon as Sunday he could reach 6,000 yards and 60 touchdowns in his career. If he does, he'll be just the third player in NFL history to reach those benchmarks within his first three NFL seasons.

The others were Broncos Hall of Famer Terrell Davis, who had 7,594 scrimmage yards and 61 touchdowns in his first four NFL seasons, and Chargers Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson, who had 7,921 scrimmage yards and 60 touchdowns in his first four NFL seasons.

Gibbs has 890 yards from scrimmage this season, which puts him on pace for 2,522 yards in 17 games. That would break the all-time NFL record of 2,509 scrimmage yards in a season, set by Chris Johnson in 2009.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. on his critics: They'll be quiet soon
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Upset about not getting a contract extension before the season, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. didn't play in four games with the Steelers.
item.content:encoded:
Upset about not getting a contract extension before the season, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. didn't play in four games with the Steelers. He was inactive with his on-again, off-again back issue, which wasn't an issue after the Cowboys traded for him.

Porter played for the Cowboys three days after the trade, but he was inactive the following week after an unexpected illness knocked him out. It prompted questions about whether he was all-in with the Cowboys, who made clear they aren't giving him a new deal this season.

Richard Sherman said on Amazon Prime Video, "I think maybe if [the Cowboys] had given him a new contract, he’d have been a little healthier today."

Porter heard the speculation, but he is unbothered.

“Me personally, I know the real,” Porter told Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. “I know the truth. I don’t really pay too much attention online to what they have to say. I just got to keep doing my job on Sundays. Once they see the tape, they’ll know. They’ll be quiet soon.”

Porter has allowed only one catch for 5 yards on nine targets in three games. He has been the lockdown corner the Cowboys expected when they sent a 2027 sixth-round draft pick and a 2028 second-round draft pick to the Steelers.

“It’s nothing new for me,” Porter told Harris. “I think I’ve always been capable of such. I feel like the tape from the last couple of years showed the same thing. I just keep the main thing the main thing.”

item.title: Steelers-Saints in Paris generates 7.7 million on Sunday morning
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday morning football doesn't do the same numbers as Sunday afternoon or evening (or Monday night or Thursday) football, but it does better than anything else on TV at that time of day.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday morning football doesn't do the same numbers as Sunday afternoon or evening (or Monday night or Thursday) football, but it does better than anything else on TV at that time of day.

The Week 7 game between the Steelers and Saints averaged 7.7 million viewers, per ESPN.

The fourth straight Sunday morning game drew the third-highest audience for any international game on NFL Network.

The four European games played in October (three in London, one in France) averaged 7.1 million viewers on NFLN.

The only problem with early-morning football (which will proliferate if/when the NFL secures the ability to stage 16 international games per year) is that it renders the Sunday morning pregame shows irrelevant. As more and more games are played at 9:30 a.m. ET, the networks may reconsider whether they even want to have pregame shows.

That said, the networks televising Sunday afternoon games need a studio presence for updates and halftimes. But the noon ET to 1:00 p.m. ET pregame shows will get smaller and smaller audiences as more and more games are played on Sunday morning.

item.title: Alabama dismisses CB Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. after arrest for doxxing, harassing police officer
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Alabama cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick Jr., the son of former NFL cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick, has been dismissed from the team.
item.content:encoded:
Alabama cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick Jr., the son of former NFL cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick, has been dismissed from the team.

Coach Kalen DeBoer announced the move on Tuesday, via Alex Scarborough of ESPN.

Kirkpatrick Jr. was arrested on Friday for doxxing and making harassing communications with a police officer. He had been suspended before Saturday's game against Texas A&M. The officer had been involved in a 2025 arrest of Kirkpatrick Jr. for reckless endangerment, attempting to elude police and speeding. Alabama suspended him in October 2025. He did not play again last season.

More recently, Kirkpatrick Jr. allegedly texted the officer, among other things, "text me back don't be no bitch!" Kirkpatrick Jr. also allegedly posted a photo of the officer and his family on Facebook.

"After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program," DeBoer said in a statement. "He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players."

Separately, Kirkpatrick Jr. is facing a misdemeanor charge from June 2026 of leaving the scene of an accident.

Dre Kirkpatrick Sr. was a first-round pick of the Bengals in 2012. He spent 10 seasons in the NFL with Cincinnati, Arizona, and San Francisco.

Kirkpatrick Jr., who was a second-string defensive back, joined Alabama in 2024.

item.title: Jared Goff backs Dan Campbell's decision to go for it deep in Lions' own end
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 in a tie game with 4:53 left, and Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for a 2-yard loss.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 in a tie game with 4:53 left, and Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for a 2-yard loss. Lions coach Dan Campbell has faced questions about his unconventional decision.

Campbell explained that the Lions had more confidence in their ability to gain 1 yard than risk Jordan Love executing a 4-minute, game-winning touchdown drive. Campbell added that, even if Detroit's fourth-down gamble failed, the Packers would not be able to run the clock out, leaving the Lions time to respond.

It worked out as D.J. Wonnum blocked the chip-shot field goal of Packers rookie kicker Trey Smack, and the Lions won on a last-play field goal.

Quarterback Jared Goff said he didn't "even think twice" when he heard the Lions were going for it deep in their own end.

"I think it’s so -- I don't know the right word — exposing of people who think it’s not the right decision just because it’s in our territory," Goff said Tuesday on 97.1 The Ticket. "It’s guaranteeing us a chance to win the game no matter what. Whereas, if we punt it, they can do exactly what we did to them on the final drive, and I’m sure they wish they had another chance to touch the ball.

"So it’s funny. I think back to a few years ago where we went for that fourth down against Green Bay in a similar situation, fourth-and-1, and we got it with David Montgomery. There was backlash on that, and we converted. I guess no matter what, there will be backlash, so who really cares at this point, right?"

In 2024, the Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 at the Green Bay 21 with 43 seconds left. David Montgomery ran for 7 yards, and Jake Bates kicked a 35-yard field goal on the final play for a 34-31 win.

"I think when we’re in those situations, we’re so much more comfortable in them than the other teams because we do them more often," Goff said, "and it is an advantage for us. It’s something that we practice and something that we spend a lot of time on, and we feel very comfortable in those situations."

The Lions lead the NFL in fourth-down conversions (89) over the past five seasons and rank second in attempts (154), according to 97.1 The Ticket. Their conversion rate of 57.8 percent over that stretch ranks seventh.

The Lions have converted 61.5 percent of their 13 fourth-down attempts this season.

"Again, unfortunately we didn’t convert this one," said Goff. "We want to get the first down and keep the game moving and finish the game on that drive, but Dan knew that if we were not to get it, OK, they’ll either kick a field goal or they’ll score a touchdown, and then we’ll get the ball back. Now, thankfully, they missed the field goal, and everything was great, but by every measure of everything, it’s the right decision."

item.title: Micah Parsons moves closer to a return
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Packers' defense could be getting a major boost.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers' defense could be getting a major boost.

Linebacker Micah Parsons, who suffered a torn ACL in December 2025, seems to be moving closer to a return.

Parsons remains on the reserve/Physically Unable to Perform list. The Packers can open a three-week practice window at any time. At the end of the three weeks, he must either move to the 53-man roster or return to the PUP list and not play this season.

On Tuesday, coach Matt LaFleur was asked whether Parsons will return to practice next week.

“I sure hope so,” LaFleur said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. As Demovsky notes, LaFleur's previous responses to that question "had been a hard no."

Parsons tore his ACL on December 14, the same day Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered the same injury. But it's very different for a quarterback and a front-seven defender. Parsons will be constantly navigating plenty of bodies and limbs, which inevitably will be hitting his legs and knees. He needs to be sure that he'll have the confidence in the repaired ACL before he takes the field again.

Green Bay could use the boost defensively. At 4-3, they host the Panthers on Thursday night. After that, they face the Patriots and Vikings before the Week 11 bye.

Given the three-week practice window, a return next week could mean that Parsons will return in Week 12, when the Packers visit the Rams in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game.

item.title: Cardinals sign WR Zay Jones
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Zay Jones was one of four wide receivers who tried out for the Cardinals on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Zay Jones was one of four wide receivers who tried out for the Cardinals on Tuesday. He joined Ronnie Bell, James Proche and Xavier Guillory on the practice field.

The Cardinals are signing Jones, according to multiple reports.

It is unclear whether Jones is joining the practice squad or the active roster, but the team announced it placed wide receiver Jalen Brooks on season-ending injured reserve on Tuesday. The Cardinals were already thin at the position after the trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. on Oct. 11.

Jones, 31, has played nine NFL seasons, including a previous stint with the Cardinals. He appeared in 11 games for the Cardinals in 2024 and eight last season, missing time for a suspension in 2024 and for a torn Achilles in 2025.

He has 20 receptions for 267 yards with the team.

Jones became a free agent in August when the Texans cut him out of the preseason.
